items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Because when he was playing with Fletcher Henderson he was the rompiest, stompiest saxophone player I ever saw.

ctx.x: McKinney's Cotton Pickers or either Fletcher Henderson, one or the other. They played somewhere together. And Coleman Hawkins... See, Coleman Hawkins changed his style about three times. Because, you see, I idolized him as a saxophone player. Because when he was playing with Fletcher Henderson he was the rompiest, stompiest saxophone player I ever saw. He could break up a house just rompin' and stompin'. Yeah, and he stomped his foot around any (?) he was playing all at the same time.

Now, remember, Coleman hawkins was the first guy that played tenor saxophone. The tenor saxophone was a bastard instrument! -- until he picked it up. Nobody wanted it. I don't think there was... I'll have to check this back in the archives somewhere. I don't think there was even a tenor in the band until Coleman played tenor. And when he come out with this tenor saxophone, it was something... It was a new deal!
